summary: Liquidity has fallen from $196.1 million at end‑2022 to $73.6 million at end‑Q3 2023, eroding the buffer. No other covenant shows a material shift. Therefore only the minimum liquidity covenant warrants tightening.

clauses.rationale: No evidence indicates the leverage ratio covenant needs adjustment.
No evidence indicates the senior secured leverage ratio covenant needs adjustment.
Liquidity declined sharply, showing reduced buffer; evidence shows falling cash and availability.
clauses.change: Increase the minimum liquidity threshold (require liquidity not less than a higher amount).

evidence.quote: Total Available Liquidity, defined as cash and cash equivalents, including restricted cash, plus availability under our short-term revolving credit facilities totaled approximately $196.1 million.
Total Available Liquidity, defined as unrestricted cash plus availability under floor plan credit facilities for inventory on hand at September 30, 2023, totaled approximately $73.6 million.

clauses.rationale: No evidence indicates the financial reporting covenant needs adjustment.
No evidence indicates the compliance certificate covenant needs adjustment.
No evidence indicates the notice of default covenant needs adjustment.

drift_reasons: Evidence of declining liquidity justifies tightening the minimum liquidity covenant, altering risk coverage.
